title: Levodopa for Parkinson's
description: Levodopa (L-dopa) is a medicine for Parkinson's disease, in which dopamine is depleted in the circuits that control movement. One study scanned people in the early stage of Parkinson's, who had never taken the medicine, while they touched their thumb to their fingers, before and after a single dose. Before the dose, the motor cortex and the supplementary motor area were less active than in people without Parkinson's; after it, both became more active and movement improved. In the first part, brightness shows the difference from people without Parkinson's; in "What changed" it shows the change since before the dose.
caveat: All findings come from one study of 8 people with early Parkinson's affecting one side of the body, and 10 people without it, scanned repeatedly every 20 minutes after a single dose. The motor cortex finding is on the side opposite the affected hand; the abstract does not say which side that was for each person, so drawing both sides is an assumption. The authors say earlier studies found the same reversal in the supplementary motor area, while the motor cortex finding has been controversial; those earlier studies were not read here. These are averages across groups of people, not a picture of any one person's brain. Treatments help many people, not everyone, and in different ways. This is not medical advice: talk to a doctor or therapist about what is right for you.

phases.name: Before treatment
phases.caption: Before the dose, during a finger movement task, the motor cortex and the supplementary motor area are less active than in people without Parkinson's.

phases.name: One dose of levodopa
phases.caption: A single dose of levodopa, then repeated scans every 20 minutes. The brain is drawn at rest here.

citations.authors: Buhmann C, Glauche V, Stürenburg HJ, Oechsner M, Weiller C, Büchel C
citations.title: Pharmacologically modulated fMRI--cortical responsiveness to levodopa in drug-naive hemiparkinsonian patients.
citations.quote: Patients performed a simple, auditory-paced random finger- opposition task every 3 s before and repeatedly every 20 min after intake of 300 mg of fast-release L-dopa.

phases.name: What changed
phases.caption: After the dose, the motor cortex and the supplementary motor area are more active during the same finger task, and movement is better. The two went closely together.

order.rationale: This last part is a summary of what the studies did not find or did not measure, not a later point in time.
